key_insight: Two-frequency cylinder oscillations break the symmetric steady-streaming pattern and create directional pumping, with the strength set by the amplitude ratio and phase difference.
engineering_relevance: This provides a tunable mechanism for lab-on-a-chip pumping, where flow direction and magnitude can be controlled without moving parts.
method: Reduced the two-frequency asymptotic problem to a sequence of 1D boundary-value problems on an annulus.
Solved the reduced problems numerically to map force dependence on amplitude ratio, phase, and Reynolds number.
Validated the annulus proxy by comparing against direct simulations in a rectangular channel.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an explicit force law for frequency ratio 2 and shows that channel flux is directly proportional to annulus force across all tested parameter ranges.
watch_item: The force-to-flux proxy was tested numerically in specific geometries and parameter ranges, so transferability to other layouts or operating regimes may need verification.
paper_title: Pumping by Two-frequency Steady Streaming: Impact of Amplitude Ratio and Phase
